title: BoardGameGeek Shelf-of-Shame Growth
dataSources: BoardGameGeek plays (`bgg:play`), Poker Now sessions (`pokernow:session`), Bridge Base Online boards (`bridgebase:board`), and Lichess tournament rounds (`lichess:tournament`).
app: BoardGameGeek play logs, Poker Now session exports, Bridge Base Online boards, and Lichess tournament data ingested into Splunk.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=bgg:play own_status=owned
| stats max(last_played_epoch) as last_played_epoch by game_name
| eval days_since_played=round((now()-last_played_epoch)/86400,1)
| where days_since_played>180
| sort - days_since_played
description: Lists owned games that have not hit the table in more than six months.
value: The shelf of shame is harmless fun until it becomes a buying signal detached from actual play.
implementation: Combine BGG collection ownership and play history, then flag titles whose last play date is older than your tolerance.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Board & Card Games — typical feeds: BoardGameGeek plays (`bgg:play`), Poker Now sessions (`pokernow:session`), Bridge Base Online boards (`bridgebase:board`), and Lichess tournament rounds (`lichess:tournament`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `bgg:play`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=bgg:play`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** BoardGameGeek play logs, Poker Now session exports, Bridge Base Online boards, and Lichess tournament data ingested into Splunk..

**Author notes:** Combine BGG collection ownership and play history, then flag titles whose last play date is older than your tolerance.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "bgg:play", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=bgg:play earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **BoardGameGeek Shelf-of-Shame Growth** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=bgg:play`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `days_since_played` (> 180) after max — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `days_since_played`, `game_name`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=bgg:play own_status=owned
| stats max(last_played_epoch) as last_played_epoch by game_name
| eval days_since_played=round((now()-last_played_epoch)/86400,1)
| where days_since_played>180
| sort - days_since_played
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=bgg:play earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table days_since_played, game_name
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=bgg:play earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `days_since_played` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=bgg:play earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(days_since_played) AS p50 perc90(days_since_played) AS p90 perc99(days_since_played) AS p99 max(days_since_played) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.66.1: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Table Of Owned Games By Days Since Last Play (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `bgg:play` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=bgg:play | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
